name: Focus management
explanation: Moving keyboard focus into a dialog when it opens, keeping it inside while it is open, and returning it to the button that opened it when it closes.
triggers: focus;tab key;keyboard users;cursor jumps;put the cursor;focus the first field;cursor in the first
requirements: Move focus to the first useful element when the component opens;Keep Tab and Shift+Tab cycling inside it while it is open;Return focus to the element that opened it when it closes;Show a clearly visible focus outline
done_when: The whole flow works with only the keyboard;Focus never jumps to the top of the page after closing

name: Keyboard navigation
explanation: Making every interactive element reachable and usable with the keyboard alone, in a logical order.
triggers: keyboard;without a mouse;tab through;keyboard only;arrow keys
requirements: Make every interactive element reachable with Tab, in a logical order;Use real buttons and links, or give custom controls tabindex and key handlers;Show a clearly visible focus outline;Use arrow keys inside menus, tabs and lists, and Tab to move between them;Never trap focus, except inside an open dialog
done_when: The whole page can be used without a mouse;You can always see where the keyboard focus is

name: ARIA attributes
explanation: HTML attributes such as role and aria-label that describe elements to screen readers and other assistive technologies.
triggers: screen reader;blind users;assistive technology;read aloud;accessible
requirements: Prefer native HTML elements such as button, a and input over ARIA roles;Give every control an accessible name, from visible text, aria-label or aria-labelledby;Keep states such as aria-expanded, aria-selected and aria-checked in sync with the UI;Hide decorative icons with aria-hidden=true, but never hide focusable elements;Do not add roles that conflict with an element's native meaning;Make the accessible name contain the visible label, ideally at the start
done_when: A screen reader announces each control's name, role and state correctly;Automated checks such as axe report no ARIA errors

name: Color contrast
explanation: Making sure text and controls stand out enough from their background to be readable, measured against WCAG contrast ratios.
triggers: hard to read;readable;low vision;text is not visible;contrast;colors look faded
requirements: Give normal text a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background;Give large text (24px, or about 19px bold) a contrast ratio of at least 3:1;Give icons, input borders and focus indicators at least 3:1 against nearby colours;Never use colour alone to show meaning, such as errors or required fields;Check contrast in every theme and in hover and focus states (disabled controls are exempt but should stay legible)
done_when: A contrast checker passes all text and controls;Errors and states are still clear in greyscale

name: Reduced motion
explanation: Respecting the user's operating-system setting to minimise animation, using the prefers-reduced-motion media query.
triggers: less animation;motion sickness;turn off animation;too much animation;dizzy
requirements: Wrap non-essential animation in a prefers-reduced-motion media query;Replace sliding, zooming and parallax with a simple fade or no animation;Stop auto-playing animations and videos, or give them a pause control;Keep essential feedback such as loading indicators, just calmer;Never flash more than three times per second
done_when: With reduced motion turned on in the system, nothing slides, zooms or bounces;All features still work the same with reduced motion

name: Accessible page structure
explanation: The basic structure every page needs to be usable by everyone: title, language, landmarks, headings and links.
triggers: screen reader friendly;make the page accessible;accessible website;wcag;a11y;skip to content;headings in order;link text;click here links;accessibility audit;work with a screen reader;whole website
requirements: Give every page a unique, descriptive title;Set the page language with the lang attribute, and mark text in other languages;Use the landmarks header, nav, main and footer, with exactly one main;Outline the page with headings in order, starting with one h1;Add a Skip to main content link as the first focusable element;Use real links whose text says where they go, never just click here;Use real text instead of images of text, and never refer to things only by shape, colour or position;Put help and contact links in the same place on every page
done_when: Screen reader users can jump to every part of the page by headings and landmarks;The first Tab press reaches the skip link, which moves focus to the main content;Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of their content

name: Accessible forms
explanation: Forms that everyone can fill in: labelled fields, clear instructions, autofill and no surprises.
triggers: label the fields;form for screen readers;accessible form;fields without labels;autofill the address;sign up form;checkout form;contact form;form should work;autofill
requirements: Give every field a visible label, connected with label for or aria-labelledby;Group related fields, such as radio buttons, with fieldset and legend;Explain required fields and formats before the user types;Add autocomplete attributes such as email, name and street-address to personal data fields;Never submit, navigate or change the page just because a field gets focus or a new value;Do not ask for information already given in the same process, unless you fill it in or let users pick it;Let users review and correct legal, financial or data-changing submissions before they are final;Make fields and their labels at least 24 pixels tall to tap
done_when: Clicking a label focuses its field, and screen readers read the label of every field;Browsers can autofill name, email and address fields

name: Accessible video and audio
explanation: Video and audio that everyone can follow: captions, transcripts, audio description and controls.
triggers: add a video;embed a video;podcast player;autoplay video;background video;live stream;add subtitles
requirements: Add captions to every video with speech, and live captions to live video;Provide a transcript for audio-only content, and a text or audio alternative for video-only content;Describe important visual information with audio description or a described version;Never autoplay sound, or offer a way to pause or mute it at once;Make the player's controls work with the keyboard and screen readers;Never flash more than three times per second
done_when: Every video can be followed with the sound off, using captions;Every control of the player works with only the keyboard

name: Visually hidden text
explanation: Text that screen readers read out but that is not shown on screen, used to add context such as which item a Delete button deletes.
triggers: only for screen readers;hidden text for screen readers;hide but keep accessible;hidden label;invisible to sighted users
requirements: Use the standard visually-hidden CSS, not display none or the hidden attribute, which hide it from screen readers too;Use it for extra context, such as Delete invoice 42 on a Delete button;Prefer visible text where it helps everyone;Make skip links and other hidden focusable elements visible when they get focus;Keep the visible words at the start of the accessible name, so voice control users can say them
done_when: Screen readers read the hidden text while it stays invisible;Nothing invisible ever receives keyboard focus;Voice control users can activate controls by saying their visible label

name: Visible focus indicator
explanation: A clear outline or highlight that shows which button, link or field the keyboard is on. Without it, keyboard users cannot tell where they are on the page.
triggers: outline disappeared;cannot see where I am when tabbing;remove the blue outline;outline on click looks ugly;custom focus style;tab highlight is invisible
requirements: Never set outline none without giving a replacement focus style;Use :focus-visible to show the ring for keyboard use and hide it after mouse clicks;Make the indicator at least as large as a 2 CSS pixel thick outline around the control;Give the focus indicator at least 3:1 contrast against the unfocused state and nearby colours;Do not rely on box-shadow alone, since forced colours modes remove it;Check focus styles on every component, including custom controls and links inside text
done_when: Tabbing through every page shows a clearly visible indicator on each focusable element;The focus ring stays visible on dark, light and image backgrounds;The indicator is still visible in Windows High Contrast mode

name: Focus not hidden by sticky content
explanation: Making sure the element that has keyboard focus is never hidden behind a sticky header, sticky footer, cookie banner, chat widget or other layer on top of the page.
triggers: tabbed button is hidden under the header;sticky header covers the link;cookie banner covers content;chat bubble hides the button;scroll focused item into view
requirements: Add scroll-padding-top and scroll-padding-bottom equal to the height of sticky headers and footers;Keep at least part of the focused element visible at all times, and ideally all of it;Let users dismiss cookie banners and chat popups, or keep them from covering page content;Close non-modal popups or move them aside when focus moves behind them;Recalculate the padding when the header height changes on small screens or zoom
done_when: Tabbing through a long page never leaves the focused element fully hidden under a sticky bar;Focused elements stay visible at 200% zoom and on a phone-sized window

name: Touch and click target size
explanation: Making buttons, links and other controls large enough, or far enough apart, that people can tap or click them without hitting the wrong one.
synonyms: target size;tap target;touch target;hit area;hit target
triggers: buttons too small to tap;tiny icons hard to click;fat finger taps;tap the wrong button;make links easier to tap;small close button
requirements: Make each target at least 24x24 CSS pixels, or space it so a 24 pixel circle centred on it overlaps no other target or circle;Aim for 44 by 44 CSS pixels for main controls and touch interfaces;Enlarge the clickable area with padding rather than making the icon bigger;Keep small icon buttons such as close, delete and edit apart from each other;Links inside a sentence are exempt, but avoid packing many tiny links together;Check targets in dense tables, toolbars and pagination
done_when: Every control passes a 24 by 24 CSS pixel size or spacing check;Close and other small icon buttons can be tapped reliably on a phone

name: Zoom, text resize and reflow
explanation: Letting people zoom the page or enlarge the text so it is easier to read, with the layout rearranging itself instead of cutting off text or needing sideways scrolling.
triggers: page breaks when zoomed in;text cut off when bigger;allow pinch to zoom;larger text setting;sideways scrolling when zoomed;increase font size
requirements: At 320 CSS pixels wide (400% zoom of a 1280 pixel window) show all content without horizontal scrolling;Let text grow to 200% without losing content or function;Never disable pinch zoom with maximum-scale or user-scalable=no;Size text in rem or em and avoid fixed heights that clip enlarged text;Keep content readable with line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter spacing 0.12 and word spacing 0.16 times the font size;Only content that needs a 2D layout, such as maps, diagrams and data tables, may scroll in both directions
done_when: At 400% zoom the page reads in a single column with no sideways scroll;At 200% text size no text overlaps or is cut off;Users can pinch to zoom on mobile

name: Accessible authentication
explanation: Letting people sign in without a memory or puzzle test, such as retyping a code or solving a puzzle, by supporting password managers, paste and other easy methods.
synonyms: cognitive function test;password manager support;captcha alternative
triggers: allow pasting the password;password manager not working;copy the one time code;login for people with memory problems;puzzle at login too hard;do not block paste
requirements: Allow paste and password manager autofill in username, password and code fields;Use autocomplete values such as username, current-password and one-time-code;Do not ask users to transcribe characters, solve puzzles or remember a code shown elsewhere unless another method exists;Offer a method with no cognitive test, such as passkeys, email links or OAuth sign-in;If a CAPTCHA is needed, offer a non-puzzle alternative or one based on recognising objects;Avoid splitting a code into one box per digit unless paste fills all boxes
done_when: Users can sign in using only a password manager and paste;Every login step has a route that needs no memory, transcription or puzzle

name: Not relying on colour alone
explanation: Showing meaning with text, icons, patterns or shapes as well as colour, so people who cannot see colours, or see them differently, still understand it.
synonyms: use of color;sensory characteristics;color blindness;colour vision deficiency
triggers: red and green status;colorblind friendly;color only error;which line is which in the chart;instructions say click the red button
requirements: Pair every status colour with a text label or icon, such as Error or a cross icon;Distinguish chart series with labels, patterns or marker shapes, not only colour;Underline links in body text, or give them 3:1 contrast with text plus a non-colour cue on hover and focus;Mark invalid fields with a message and icon, not only a red border;Never write instructions that rely only on colour, shape, size, position or sound;Check designs with a colour blindness simulator or in greyscale
done_when: All information is still clear when the page is viewed in greyscale;No instruction refers to something only by colour, shape or position

name: Image alternative text
explanation: Text that describes what an image shows or does, read out by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load. Decorative images get empty alt text so they are skipped.
synonyms: alt text;alt attribute;text alternative;image description;decorative image;images of text
triggers: describe pictures for blind users;screen reader reads the file name;missing alt;caption for screen readers;text inside an image
requirements: Give each meaningful image alt text that conveys the same information or purpose, in a short phrase;Use an empty alt attribute for purely decorative images, or put them in CSS backgrounds;For linked or button images, describe the action or destination, not the picture;Give charts and complex images a short alt plus a longer description nearby;Do not start with image of or repeat nearby caption text;Use real text instead of text in images, except logos;Give inline SVG icons role=img with a label, or aria-hidden=true when decorative
done_when: Automated checks find no img without an alt attribute;A screen reader user gets the same information as a sighted user from every image;Decorative images are silent in a screen reader

name: Alternatives to gestures and dragging
explanation: Making sure anything done by swiping, pinching, drawing a path or dragging can also be done with a simple tap or click, for people who cannot make precise movements.
synonyms: pointer gestures;dragging movements;pointer cancellation;single-pointer alternative;motion actuation
triggers: swipe only;drag and drop without a mouse;pinch to zoom alternative;reorder without dragging;cancel accidental tap
requirements: Give every multi-finger or path gesture a single tap alternative, such as plus and minus zoom buttons;Give every drag action a click alternative, such as move up and down buttons or a menu;Trigger actions on release, not on press, so users can slide off to cancel;Let users undo an action that starts on press;Give shake or tilt actions a button alternative and a way to turn motion off;Keep the alternatives reachable by keyboard and screen reader
done_when: Every feature works with single taps or clicks only;Pressing a button and sliding away before release does nothing

name: Adjustable time limits
explanation: Warning people before a session or task times out and letting them turn off, change or extend the time, so slower users do not lose their work.
triggers: session expired while typing;logged out too fast;give more time to fill in;form timed out and lost my work;are you still there
requirements: Before a time limit ends, warn users and give at least 20 seconds to extend it with one simple action;Let users extend at least 10 times, or let them turn off the limit or set it to at least 10 times the default;Tell users about time limits and inactivity timeouts at the start;Keep entered data for at least 20 hours, or save it so users can return after signing in;Make the warning a dialog that screen readers announce and the keyboard can operate;Real-time events and essential limits such as auctions are exempt, but explain them
done_when: A timeout warning appears in time and Extend keeps the user signed in;Work entered before a timeout is not lost after signing in again

name: Pause controls for autoplay and moving content
explanation: Giving people a way to pause, stop or hide anything that moves, blinks, scrolls, updates or plays sound on its own, because it distracts or blocks reading.
synonyms: pause stop hide;audio control;autoplay controls;auto-updating content
triggers: stop the slideshow;mute background music;pause the animation;ticker keeps scrolling;stop auto rotate;video plays by itself
requirements: Give moving, blinking or scrolling content that runs for over 5 seconds a pause, stop or hide control;Let users pause auto-updating content, such as feeds and tickers, or set how often it updates;Do not autoplay sound for more than 3 seconds without a pause or volume control near the start of the page;Place pause controls early in the focus order and make them work by keyboard;Stop auto-rotating carousels on hover and focus and when reduced motion is set;Keep the paused state until the user resumes
done_when: Every moving or auto-updating area can be paused with the keyboard;No sound plays on load for more than 3 seconds without a control

name: Seizure-safe flashing content
explanation: Keeping flashing and strobing effects in videos, games and animations below safe limits, because fast flashes can trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy.
synonyms: photosensitive epilepsy;three flashes;flash threshold;red flash;strobe effect
triggers: flashing lights warning;strobe in the video;epilepsy safe animation;screen flicker effect;lightning effect in the game
requirements: Never flash more than three times in any one second;If flashes are faster, keep them small and below the general and saturated red flash thresholds;Avoid saturated red flashes and fast high-contrast stripes or checkerboards;Analyse videos and effects with a flash analysis tool such as PEAT or Harding;Let users turn off or reduce flashes and screen shake in settings;Give a warning before content that cannot avoid flashing
done_when: Flash analysis passes on all videos and animated effects;No element flashes more than three times per second

name: Avoiding redundant data entry
explanation: Not making people type the same information twice in one process, for example by filling it in again for them or letting them choose it from what they entered before.
triggers: type the address twice;same as shipping address checkbox;remember what I entered;already entered this;fill in from earlier step
requirements: Fill in information the user already gave in the same process, or let them select it;Offer a Same as billing address option for repeated addresses;Keep entered data when users go back and forward between steps;Show earlier answers on a check answers page instead of asking again;Re-entry is allowed only for security, such as confirming a password, or when the earlier data is no longer valid
done_when: No step asks for data already given in the same process without filling it in;Going back to a previous step keeps everything the user typed

name: Page and content language
explanation: Declaring the language of the page, and of any passages in another language, so screen readers use the right pronunciation and translation tools work correctly.
synonyms: lang attribute;language of parts;html lang;BCP 47 language tag
triggers: screen reader wrong accent;reads in the wrong language;mixed language page;quote in another language
requirements: Set lang on the html element with a valid BCP 47 code, such as en or fr-CA;Mark passages, quotes and links in another language with their own lang attribute;Change lang when users switch the page language;Write language switcher options in their own language and mark each with lang;Set dir=rtl for right-to-left languages;Proper names, technical terms and borrowed words need no lang marking
done_when: Automated checks find a valid lang on every page;A screen reader switches pronunciation for foreign-language passages

name: Plain language content
explanation: Writing interface text and content in short, clear, everyday words, explaining jargon and abbreviations, so more people understand it quickly, including people with cognitive disabilities.
triggers: easy to understand text;too much jargon;simpler wording;write for everyone;explain abbreviations;confusing instructions
requirements: Use short sentences and common words, and put the most important point first;Explain or avoid jargon, idioms and abbreviations, expanding each abbreviation at first use;Use the same word for the same thing everywhere;Write instructions as numbered steps and use active voice;Break long text into headings, short paragraphs and lists;Offer a simpler summary when text needs more than lower secondary reading level;Test wording with real users, including people with cognitive or learning disabilities
done_when: Users can complete key tasks without asking what a word means;Every abbreviation is expanded at its first use;A readability check of key pages shows a lower secondary reading level or a simpler summary

name: High contrast (forced colours) mode support
explanation: Making sure icons, borders, focus rings and selected states stay visible when Windows High Contrast or another forced colours mode replaces the page colours with the user's own.
synonyms: forced colors;windows high contrast;contrast themes;forced-color-adjust;system colors
triggers: invisible in high contrast mode;icons disappear in dark contrast theme;windows contrast theme;custom checkbox not visible in high contrast
requirements: Use a transparent outline or border instead of box-shadow or background colour alone for focus and boundaries;Draw SVG icons with currentColor so they follow the system text colour;Show selected and disabled states with borders or system colors such as Highlight and GrayText;Use the forced-colors media query only to fix problems, not to restyle everything;Use forced-color-adjust none only on small parts that must keep their colours, such as colour swatches;Test in Windows contrast themes or with forced colours emulation in browser developer tools
done_when: All controls, icons and focus rings are visible in light and dark contrast themes;Selected tabs and checked items are distinguishable in forced colours mode

name: Descriptive link text
explanation: Writing link text that says where a link goes or what it does, instead of click here or read more, so people scanning a list of links understand each one.
triggers: read more links;more information link;opens in a new tab warning;link to a pdf;same link text different pages
requirements: Make the link text describe the destination or action, such as Download the 2025 annual report;Avoid click here, read more and here, or add hidden context such as the article title;Give links with the same text the same destination;Mention when a link opens a new window or downloads a file, with its type and size;Start the accessible name with the visible link text so voice control users can say it;Use a link for navigation and a button for actions
done_when: A screen reader list of links makes sense out of context;No two links with the same text go to different places

name: Accessible client-side page changes
explanation: Making view changes in a single-page app work for keyboard and screen reader users by updating the title, moving focus sensibly and announcing that new content has loaded.
synonyms: route change announcement;spa accessibility;route focus management
triggers: screen reader does not notice page change;focus stays on old link after navigation;title does not change in single page app;announce new page
requirements: Update document.title for every view change;Move focus to the new view's h1 or main area, with tabindex=-1 on a non-focusable target;Or announce the new page title in a polite live region that already exists in the page;Announce loading and errors with role=status or role=alert;Restore focus and scroll position when the user goes back;Do not move focus for small in-page updates such as filters
done_when: Each route change announces the new page in NVDA and VoiceOver;The tab after navigation continues from the new content, not the old link;The browser tab shows the right title for each view

name: Accessibility testing
explanation: Checking a product for accessibility problems with automated scanners, keyboard and zoom checks, screen readers, and testing with disabled people.
synonyms: a11y testing;wcag evaluation;accessibility audit;screen reader testing
triggers: test with a screen reader;check if my site is accessible;run an accessibility checker;find accessibility bugs;wcag compliance check
requirements: Run automated checks such as axe or Lighthouse in development and CI, knowing they find only part of the problems;Test every key journey using only the keyboard;Check pages at 200% text size and 400% zoom;Test with screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack;Pick a representative sample of pages and states, including errors and dialogs;Record each issue with the WCAG criterion, severity and steps to reproduce;Include disabled users in usability testing
done_when: Automated scans pass in CI on key pages;Key journeys are completed using only the keyboard and with a screen reader;Each issue found is logged against a WCAG criterion

name: Accessibility statement
explanation: A public page that says how accessible a website or app is, which parts are not yet accessible and what to use instead, and how to report problems.
triggers: publish accessibility page;report an accessibility problem;known accessibility issues;public sector website requirements
requirements: State the standard and level targeted, such as WCAG 2.2 AA, and whether it is fully or partly met;List known issues, their impact and accessible alternatives;Give a contact method for feedback and a target response time;Say when and how the product was last evaluated and date the statement;Include the enforcement procedure where law requires it, such as EU public sector sites;Link the statement from every page, usually in the footer;Review and update it after audits and major releases
done_when: The statement is reachable from every page;Each known issue lists a workaround or alternative;A test feedback message reaches the team

name: Accessibility conformance report (VPAT)
explanation: A formal document, usually based on the VPAT template, that lists each accessibility requirement and says how well a product meets it, so buyers can compare products.
triggers: customer asks for a vpat;accessibility for procurement;government tender accessibility;fill in the vpat
requirements: Use the current ITI VPAT edition that matches the market: WCAG, Section 508, EU or International;Name the product, version, report date and the evaluation methods used;Rate each criterion as Supports, Partially Supports, Does Not Support or Not Applicable;Explain every partial or failing rating in the remarks with its impact;Base the ratings on real testing, not assumptions;Update the report for each major release
done_when: Every criterion in the chosen standard has a rating and remarks where needed;Ratings match the results of a recent accessibility test

name: Accessible PDF and documents
explanation: PDFs and office documents built so screen readers can read them: tagged structure, correct reading order, headings, alt text, a title and a language.
triggers: make pdf readable by screen reader;export accessible pdf;scanned pdf for blind users;pdf reading order wrong
requirements: Create documents with real headings, lists and table headers, then export to tagged PDF;Set a document title and show it in the title bar, and set the document language;Give images alt text and mark decorative content as artifacts;Check the reading order and tab order follow the visual order;Mark table header cells and keep tables simple;Run OCR on scanned pages and give form fields labels;Validate with a checker such as PAC or the Acrobat accessibility check, and offer an HTML version when possible
done_when: An accessibility checker reports no PDF/UA errors;A screen reader reads the document in the correct order with headings and image descriptions
